_note: Tier 0 fixture - Divorce, CONTESTED variant - RULING 13 part 3 (§ 6.5.7). The FOURTH variant, and its own variant rather than an overload of `blank-b`, because a variant carrying two independent traps cannot attribute its own failure. `canProceed()` (`:749-766`) admits exactly two step-1 states; `voluntary`+`mediationMode:"new"` is the other three variants and this is the second. The two arms PARTITION the payload: under `voluntary` the `court` pair is always `""`; under `contested` the whole `mediation` object except `mediation_record_no`, plus `custody_arrangement` / `custody_reference` / `children`, is always `""` - `hasChildren`'s toggle lives at `:1288` inside `isVoluntary && mediationMode === "new"` and cannot be reached from here. Without this variant one of those two groups is only ever empty and A PORT THAT HARDCODED `""` THERE PASSES TIER 0 - the `F0-AC-86` vacuity shape. The `mediation`, `children` and `hasChildren` keys are therefore REMOVED, not blanked: § 6.5.3 item 7 classes them `unreachable` from this state and a fixture may not declare an unreachable key. Their oracle leaves are still emitted as `""`, sourced from `:634-637` / `:638` / `:639`. Spouses stay ASYMMETRIC (§ 6.5.3 item 1a) so the `both()` mirror's discard of the wife's value is observable on this arm too. Synthetic throughout: no real citizen data, no real UIN, no token (F0-AC-70 item 2). Locale seed: lo.
